audit_question: Audit whether the current HSConfig repo remains maintainable and slim, with clear command-handler boundaries, credible test coverage, synced operator-skill surfaces, controlled dependencies, manageable research noise, and a clear next-work recommendation.
primary_sources: Command: python scripts/sync_installed_skill.py --check -> HSConfig skill is in sync: C:/Users/darbo/.codex/skills/hsconfig

Command: python -m pytest tests/test_skill_files.py tests/test_docs_active_path.py tests/test_scope_boundaries.py tests/test_operator_summary.py tests/test_apply_gate.py tests/test_runtime_apply.py tests/test_archetype_fixture_matrix.py tests/test_matrix_current_truth.py -q -> 135 passed
confirmed_facts: The runtime dependency footprint is intentionally small: pyproject.toml declares hearthstone as the only runtime dependency and pytest as the dev dependency.
The CLI exposes a normal path of source-manifest, draft-source-documents, research-deck, prepare, and apply while keeping build/research-contract/expert inputs separate.
Command handler extraction exists under src/hsconfig/commands, so the repo is no longer a single monolithic CLI file.
The installed HSConfig skill is synchronized from the repo source by scripts/sync_installed_skill.py, and --check passes in the current workspace.
The active README and operator docs point to docs/operator/README.md and keep HSConfig pre-run-only.
The focused skill/operator/gate/matrix test slice passed with 135 tests, and the full suite passed with 574 passed and 2 skipped.
The provided deck set is governed by an 11-deck representative matrix plus CuteWarrior as supplemental, avoiding uncontrolled fixture widening.
The repo contains many historical docs/superpowers plans and docs/research packages. They are evidence/history, but they add search and reading noise for future agents.
strengths: The product boundary is clear: HSConfig is a pre-run direct-config builder, not a post-run tuner.
Operator docs, skill docs, and CLI help agree on the normal path.
The dependency footprint is slim for a Hearthstone deck-code/config compiler.
The installed skill parity check is explicit and currently passing.
Tests cover docs, skill sync, scope boundaries, operator summary, apply gate, runtime apply, fixture matrix truth, and end-to-end package behavior.
gaps_or_risks: Historical research and plan volume is the biggest remaining slimness issue. It does not break the normal path, but it increases search noise.
More cleanup could improve agent efficiency by indexing or archiving old docs more aggressively without deleting evidence.
The CLI has been split into command modules, but further tiny extractions should be done only when they reduce actual complexity; broad refactors would add churn.
The current audit package is intentionally uncommitted during brainstorming. If accepted as evidence, it should be committed or removed to keep git status clean.
deck_set_implications: The current repo is maintainable enough for the provided deck set. Do not add CuteWarrior as a twelfth representative row yet; keep it supplemental until Kingslayer and Boarlock are either closed or explicitly preserved as durable source-informed controls.
recommendation: No urgent architecture rewrite is needed. The next best work is a small cleanup-plus-closure wave: keep the product code stable, archive/index noisy historical research more clearly, then close Boarlock Fracking or Kingslayer Quick Pick source-depth gaps. Avoid new surfaces and avoid broad CLI refactors unless a specific test or operator path becomes hard to maintain.
